UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S MOTION UNDER RULE 26(d)(1) FOR PRESENT AUTHORIZATION TO SERVE TWO INTERROGATORIES ON META CONCERNING PLAINTIFF’S FULL LEGAL NAME AND FACEBOOK ACCOUNT

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1) for an order authorizing him to serve on Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”), before the Rule 26(f) conference, the two interrogatories in the attached Exhibit A — Meta — November 7, 2026 — Final (“Exhibit A”). A Memorandum in Support under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1), the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with its Exhibit 1 (“Ballentine Decl.”), a Proposed Order with a separate alternative referral disposition, and a Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument and Request for Prompt Determination on the Papers accompany this Motion.

1.	The relief requested. Plaintiff asks the Court to authorize service of the exact Exhibit A as an express, limited exception to the discovery posture described in ECF No. 108, and notwithstanding the denial of the prior requests in ECF No. 84. Meta is the sole discovery respondent. Interrogatory No. 1 asks whether Meta submitted to NCMEC, between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, inclusive, any CyberTipline report that, as submitted by Meta, contained or otherwise identified the full legal name “Marvelle J. Ballentine.” Interrogatory No. 2 asks whether Meta submitted to NCMEC, in the same period, any CyberTipline report in connection with the Facebook account associated with Plaintiff and enforced against on or about July 4, 2022. Each question admits three answers: “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable to determine after reasonable inquiry.” The two questions are independent. Neither answer is conditioned on the other. This application does not await any answer from NCMEC.

2.	Timing of service and answers. Plaintiff asks that the order direct him to serve Exhibit A within three days after entry, and direct Meta to serve verified answers and any specific objections within seven days after that service, or within the definite period the Court fixes. Plaintiff asks that Meta answer through an officer or agent furnishing information available to the organization under Rule 33(b)(1)(B), under oath under Rule 33(b)(3), with any objection stated with specificity under Rule 33(b)(4), and with the signatures Rule 33(b)(5) requires. These periods govern the authorized discovery. They do not shorten the briefing on this Motion.

3.	The earlier orders and the changed scope. On October 7, 2026, the Court denied Plaintiff’s earlier motions to serve three interrogatories on NCMEC and four on Meta “as premature,” stating that discovery “officially begins when the District Judge issues a Scheduling Order.” ECF No. 84 at 1–2. On October 29, 2026, the Court stated that “the District Judge has chosen to refrain from beginning any discovery until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss.” ECF No. 108 at 2. This is a new application for present authorization. The earlier Meta request asked four questions, including alias and email questions with a conditional-answer design. Those questions are retired. The full-name question now reaches any qualifying Meta submission in the stated period, not only the two reports described in the April 22, 2026 letters or the specified account. The account question addresses the inquiry Meta’s own memorandum describes. ECF No. 22 at 4, 6. The full-name subject appeared before; the scope and the present-harm showing are new. This Motion contains no Rule 54(b) request and seeks no vacatur of any prior order.

4.	The grounds. The association between Plaintiff’s full legal name and two CyberTipline reports is already in the public litigation record. Plaintiff has never seen a report and does not know whether any original report contains his full legal name. Ballentine Decl. ¶¶ 5–6. The unresolved association affects his present decisions about retaining counsel and participating openly in professional work. Id. ¶¶ 8–16. Meta controls its own submission records. Meta seeks dismissal with prejudice, ECF No. 22 at 14, proposes discovery only after the claims survive, ECF No. 73 at 4, and ordinary discovery remains deferred, ECF No. 108 at 2. That sequence risks ending ordinary discovery in this action before Plaintiff receives either answer. The Memorandum develops two routes to the same relief: the modified preliminary-injunction test that courts in this District apply to expedited discovery, Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. v. Markfeld, No. 3:25-cv-00885-RCY, ECF No. 70 at 17–18 (E.D. Va. July 29, 2026); Shenzhenshibairihongmaoyiyouxiangongsi v. Novoluto GmbH, No. 3:25-cv-00844-RCY, ECF No. 44 at 3–4 (E.D. Va. Mar. 9, 2026), and, independently, good cause. The element analysis is in the Memorandum.

5.	Determination by the District Judge or express referral. ECF No. 108 attributes the deferral to the District Judge’s choice. Plaintiff therefore asks the District Judge to determine this application. If the District Judge refers it, Plaintiff asks that the referral expressly authorize the Magistrate Judge to determine the limited exception under Rule 26(d)(1), including its timing and any response period. If the application is before the Magistrate Judge and he regards the deferral as reserving the question, Plaintiff asks that he state that understanding and present the limited-exception request to the District Judge. This is a case-management request. It asserts no power to choose the judicial officer.

6.	Submission and priority. Plaintiff waives oral argument and requests prompt determination upon completion of briefing, subject to the Court’s directions. To the extent an adverse disposition would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by Exhibit A, Plaintiff requests that the Court resolve this authorization request before or expressly within that disposition. Plaintiff requests no general stay of the dismissal motions and no shortened response period.

7.	Local Civil Rule 37(E) statement. [Complete from the actual November 9, 2026 conference, or the documented attempts, with counsel for Meta: the date and Eastern time; the means, by telephone or in person; the participants; the exact Exhibit A questions presented; the request for voluntary answers; counsel’s position on each question; counsel’s statements on whether Meta’s submission records can be searched by full name and by the specified account, and on the search steps, time, or expense involved; the proposed seven-day period or another period; any burden, privilege, or confidentiality ground stated; counsel’s position on the modified test and on good cause; counsel’s position on Plaintiff’s waiver of oral argument and request for determination on the papers; and each point left unresolved. State agreement only where counsel expressed it. An email arranging a call is not a completed conference.] The Ballentine Declaration, ¶¶ 17–19, records the same conference.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter the accompanying Proposed Order:

(a)	authorizing Plaintiff, under Rule 26(d)(1), as an express and limited exception to the discovery posture described in ECF No. 108 and notwithstanding ECF No. 84, to serve on Meta, before the Rule 26(f) conference, the two interrogatories in Exhibit A — Meta — November 7, 2026 — Final, in the form attached;

(b)	directing Plaintiff to serve Exhibit A within three days after entry;

(c)	directing Meta to serve its answers and any objections within seven days after that service, or within another definite period the Court fixes;

(d)	requiring that Meta answer through an officer or agent under Rule 33(b)(1)(B), under oath under Rule 33(b)(3), state any objection with specificity under Rule 33(b)(4) and answer to the extent not objected to, and sign as Rule 33(b)(5) requires, subject to the answer and content limits stated in Exhibit A;

(e)	determining this application in the first instance or, if referred, expressly authorizing the Magistrate Judge to determine the limited exception under Rule 26(d)(1), including its timing and any response period; and

(f)	determining this application promptly on the papers upon completion of briefing and, to the extent an adverse disposition would depend on the specific reporting fact addressed by Exhibit A, resolving this application before or expressly within that disposition.
